p.src: Wu Yong said to Song Jiang, “Today, by great good fortune, you have come through unharmed, brother, and Physician An is here in the stronghold to attend to your illness. This is an immense blessing for Liangshan Marsh. While you lay ill, brother, I repeatedly sent men to Daming to learn what was happening. Grand Secretary Liang was anxious and alarmed day and night, fearing only that our army might descend upon the city. I also sent men throughout the streets and marketplaces inside and outside Beijing to post anonymous proclamations everywhere, informing the inhabitants that they need not be alarmed. Every wrong has its culprit and every debt its debtor; when our great army reaches the prefecture, it will seek only those responsible. Because of this, Grand Secretary Liang grew even more uneasy and suspicious. In the Eastern Capital, Grand Preceptor Cai heard that Guan Sheng had surrendered, and no longer dared mention the matter before the emperor. He advocates only that we be granted amnesty, so that everyone may be left in peace. He has therefore written repeatedly to Grand Secretary Liang, instructing him to spare Lu Junyi and Shi Xiu for the time being, so that there may still be room to maneuver.” On hearing this, Song Jiang immediately wanted to hurry the troops down the mountain to attack Beijing. Wu Yong said, “Winter is now ending and spring beginning, and the Lantern Festival will soon be upon us. Each year Beijing puts on a magnificent display of lanterns. I mean to seize this opportunity: first we shall plant men in ambush within the city, then advance our forces from outside. Striking in concert from within and without, we can take it.” Song Jiang said, “A splendid plan! I ask our strategist to issue the orders at once.” Wu Yong said, “The first and most important task is to set a fire within the city as our signal. Which of you brothers dares go ahead with me and set that fire?” A man stepped forward below the hall and said, “I am willing to go.” When they looked, it was Shi Qian, the Flea on a Drum. Shi Qian said, “When I was young, I once went to Beijing. There is a tower in the city called the Emerald Cloud Tower. Upstairs and down, it has well over a hundred chambers, large and small. On the night of the Lantern Festival, it is certain to be packed and bustling. I shall seize an opening and slip secretly into the city. On the night of the fifteenth day of the first month, I shall climb to the top of the Emerald Cloud Tower and start a fire as the signal. Then, Strategist, you can deploy the men to break into the prison. That would be the best plan.” Wu Yong said, “That is precisely what I had in mind. At dawn tomorrow, go down the mountain ahead of us. On the night of the Lantern Festival, at the first watch, set fire to the tower. Accomplish that, and the merit will be yours.” Shi Qian accepted the command and departed.

p.src: The next day Wu Yong assigned Xie Zhen and Xie Bao to disguise themselves as hunters and enter the residences of officials in Beijing, offering them wild game. On the night of the fifteenth day of the first month, as soon as they saw the signal fire, they were to go before the Military Governor’s Office and intercept the officers and soldiers carrying reports. The two accepted their orders and departed. Next he assigned Du Qian and Song Wan to disguise themselves as traveling rice merchants, push a handcart into the city, and find lodging there. On the night of the Lantern Festival, when they saw the signal fire rise, they were to seize the eastern gate first. “That shall be the achievement entrusted to you two.” The two accepted their orders and departed. Next he assigned Kong Ming and Kong Liang to disguise themselves as servants and sleep beneath the eaves in Beijing’s busy marketplace. When they saw the fire rise before the tower, they were to move back and forth in support. The two accepted their orders and departed. Next he assigned Li Ying and Shi Jin to disguise themselves as travelers and lodge outside Beijing’s eastern gate. When they saw the signal fire within the city, they were first to kill the soldiers guarding the gate and seize it, opening a route of escape. The two accepted their orders and departed. Next he assigned Lu Zhishen and Wu Song to disguise themselves as itinerant monks and seek lodging at a monastery outside Beijing. When they saw the signal fire within the city, they were to go outside the southern gate, block the main army, and cut off its route of advance. The two accepted their orders and departed. Next he assigned Zou Yuan and Zou Run to disguise themselves as lantern sellers, go directly into Beijing, and find an inn. When they saw the fire rise from the tower, they were to go before the prison office and provide support. The two accepted their orders and departed. Next he assigned Liu Tang and Yang Xiong to disguise themselves as constables and lodge directly before the Beijing prefectural offices. When the signal fire rose, they were to intercept every messenger and prevent the defenders from supporting one another from front to rear. The two accepted their orders and departed. Next he assigned Master Gongsun Sheng to disguise himself as a wandering Daoist, with Ling Zhen dressed as his acolyte. Taking several hundred fire-and-wind and heaven-shaking cannon charges with them, they were to go directly to a secluded place inside Beijing and wait there, then set them off when they saw the signal fire. The two accepted their orders and departed. Next he assigned Zhang Shun to accompany Yan Qing into the city through the water gate, make straight for Squire Lu’s residence, and capture the adulterous woman and her lover alone. Next he assigned Wang the Short Tiger, Sun Xin, Zhang Qing, Hu Sanniang, Gu the Elder Sister, and Sun Erniang to pose as three country couples, enter the city to view the lanterns, make their way to Lu Junyi’s residence, and set it ablaze. Next he assigned Chai Jin to take Yue He with him, both disguised as military officers, and go directly to Warden Cai’s house to ensure that the two prisoners’ lives were saved. Once all assignments had been made, every chieftain accepted his orders and departed. Each was to obey the military orders strictly, without the slightest error.

p.src: It was now the beginning of the first month. Leaving aside how the heroes of Liangshan Marsh descended the mountain one after another and set forth, let us tell instead how Grand Secretary Liang of Beijing summoned Li Cheng, Wen Da, Prefect Wang, and the other officials to discuss the Lantern Festival. Grand Secretary Liang said, “By annual custom, Beijing puts on a magnificent display of lanterns to celebrate the Lantern Festival and share the festivities with the people, following precisely the practice of the Eastern Capital. But now that the Liangshan Marsh bandits have twice invaded our territory, I fear that displaying the lanterns may invite disaster. I intend to suspend the festival. What counsel do you officials have?” Wen Da promptly replied, “Those bandits have secretly withdrawn and recklessly pasted up anonymous notices. That only shows they are at their wits’ end and surely have no plan. Why need Your Excellency worry so much? If the lanterns are not displayed this year and their spies learn of it, they will certainly mock us. Your Excellency should issue an order informing the residents that there are to be more decorative lanterns than last year and additional festival performances; two more lantern mountains are to be erected in the center of the city; and, following the practice of the Eastern Capital, the night curfew is to be lifted and lanterns displayed for five nights, from the thirteenth through the seventeenth. Have the prefect inspect the residents’ preparations and permit no deficiencies. Your Excellency should personally make the springtime circuit and be sure to share the festivities with the people. I shall personally lead a body of troops out of the city and station them at Flying Tiger Ravine to guard against any treacherous scheme by the bandits. We shall also have Commander Li personally lead the armored cavalry in patrols around the city, so the residents need feel no alarm or anxiety.” Grand Secretary Liang was delighted by these words. Once the officials had settled their deliberations, they immediately posted proclamations informing the residents. Beijing’s Daming Prefecture was the foremost great prefecture and strategic center north of the Yellow River, and merchants from every circuit gathered there as thickly as clouds and mist. As soon as they heard that lanterns were to be displayed, they all came to join the festival. The ward officers responsible for every quarter, lane, and alley within the city made daily inspections, and the people had no choice but to prepare festival performances. Every wealthy household vied to display the finest decorative lanterns. Some traveled two or three hundred li to buy them, and even the nearer journeys took them a hundred li or more. There were also merchants who brought lanterns into the city every year to sell. Every family erected a lantern frame before its gate, striving to hang the finest lanterns and display ingenious fireworks. Inside, they constructed decorative pavilions and set out multicolored screens and firework lanterns, hanging famous calligraphy and paintings on every side alongside rare antiques and curios. Throughout the city, in every avenue and alley, every household was required to light lanterns. Beside the Prefectural Bridge near the Daming garrison headquarters, a great lantern mountain was erected. Two dragons of red and yellow paper coiled over it, a lamp burning on every scale, while clear water spouted from their mouths. All around, above and below the river at Prefectural Bridge, countless lamps were lit. Before the Bronze Buddha Temple another lantern mountain was erected, with a blue-green dragon coiled atop it and hundreds upon hundreds of decorative lanterns all around. Before the Emerald Cloud Tower yet another lantern mountain was erected, with a white dragon coiled upon it and countless lights burning on all four sides. This winehouse was famed throughout the lands north of the Yellow River and acclaimed as the finest of all. It had three tiers of overhanging eaves, carved beams, and ornamented pillars, and was superbly constructed. Upstairs and down were scores of private rooms; drums and music thundered to the skies all day long, and the daily din of pipes and songs filled the ears. In the Daoist and Buddhist temples throughout the city, lights were set up in every shrine hall and Dharma hall to celebrate the abundant harvest. As for the entertainment quarters and pleasure houses, there is no need even to speak of them.

p.src: The Liangshan Marsh spies obtained this news and carried it back up the mountain. Wu Yong was delighted when he heard it and went to tell Song Jiang all the particulars. Song Jiang at once wished to lead the troops in person to attack Beijing, but An Daoquan remonstrated, “General, your wound has not yet fully closed. You must on no account exert yourself rashly. Should anger disturb it even slightly, it will be very difficult to heal.” Wu Yong said, “I shall make the journey in my elder brother’s place.” He and Pei Xuan, the “Iron-Faced Registrar,” immediately assigned the troops into eight columns. In the first, Huyan Zhuo of the Twin Whips was to lead Han Tao and Peng Qi in the vanguard, with Huang Xin, “Guardian of the Three Mountains,” supporting them from the rear; all were cavalry. The man whom Huyan Zhuo had struck down in the earlier battle was a decoy; it had been a deliberate ruse to entrap Guan Sheng. In the second column, Lin Chong, the “Panther Head,” was to lead Ma Lin and Deng Fei in the vanguard, with Hua Rong, “Little Li Guang,” supporting them from the rear; all were cavalry. In the third column, Guan Sheng of the Great Blade was to lead Xuan Zan and Hao Siwen in the vanguard, with Sun Li, the “Sick Yuchi,” supporting them from the rear; all were cavalry. In the fourth column, Qin Ming, the “Thunderbolt,” was to lead Ou Peng and Yan Shun in the vanguard, with Yang Zhi, the “Blue-Faced Beast,” supporting them from the rear; all were cavalry. For the fifth column, the infantry leader Mu Hong, the “Unrestrained,” was assigned to lead Du Xing and Zheng Tianshou. In the sixth column, the infantry leader Li Kui, the “Black Whirlwind,” was to lead Li Li and Cao Zheng. In the seventh column, the infantry leader Lei Heng, the “Winged Tiger,” was to lead Shi En and Mu Chun. In the eighth column, the infantry leader Fan Rui, the “Demon King of Chaos,” was to lead Xiang Chong and Li Gun. These eight columns of horse and foot were each to take a separate road and depart at once, without the slightest delay. By the second watch on the fifteenth day of the first month, all were to reach the walls of Beijing. Cavalry and infantry set out together. The eight columns descended the mountain according to their orders, while all the remaining chieftains stayed with Song Jiang to guard the stronghold.

p.src: Now Shi Qian was a man who could fly over eaves and walk along walls. He did not enter the city by the proper road, but scaled the wall at night. The inns within the city would not lodge solitary travelers, so he wandered idly through the streets by day and, when evening came, took shelter beneath a divine image in the Temple of the Eastern Peak. On the thirteenth day of the first month, he roamed through the city watching the residents erect lantern sheds and hang up lights. While he was looking, he saw Xie Zhen and Xie Bao carrying game on shoulder poles as they wandered about observing the city. He also happened upon Du Qian and Song Wan as the two emerged from an entertainment quarter. That day Shi Qian first went up to the Emerald Cloud Tower to make a circuit. There he saw Kong Ming with his hair loose, dressed in ragged sheepskins, a staff in his right hand and a bowl in his left, filthy and foul as he begged for alms. On seeing Shi Qian, he signaled him around to the back so they could speak. Shi Qian said, “Brother, a strapping fellow like you, with such a healthy fair complexion, does not look like a beggar. There are many constables in Beijing; if one of them sees through your disguise, you will ruin our great undertaking. You had better hide yourself and keep out of sight.” Before he had finished speaking, another beggar came along by the wall. When they looked, it proved to be Kong Liang. Shi Qian said, “Brother, you too have left your face as white as snow. You do not look like a man who has endured hunger and starvation either. Looking like this, you are certain to give the game away.” He had only just finished when two men seized them sharply from behind and shouted, “A fine business you fellows are about!” When they turned to look, the men were Yang Xiong and Liu Tang. Shi Qian said, “You frightened me to death!” Yang Xiong said, “All of you, come with me.” He led them to a secluded place and reproached them: “You three have no sense at all! How could you stand there talking like that? Luckily it was we two who saw you. If some sharp-eyed, quick-handed constable had discovered you, would that not have ruined our elder brother’s great undertaking? We two have already seen everything. There is no need for any of you brothers to go out into the streets again.” Kong Ming said, “Zou Yuan and Zou Run are out in the street selling lanterns, while Lu Zhishen and Wu Song are already in a hermitage outside the city. There is nothing more to discuss. When the appointed time comes, each of us need only carry out his task.” After the five had spoken, they came out before a temple and happened upon a Daoist master emerging from within. When they raised their heads to look, it was Gongsun Sheng, the “Dragon in the Clouds,” with Ling Zhen following behind disguised as a young Daoist attendant. The seven men nodded to show that they understood, then each went his own way.

p.src: In Beijing, the fifteenth night's delights are fair; the welcome rain has cleared, and spring comes early there.

u.src: In Beijing, the fifteenth night's delights are fair; the welcome rain has cleared, and spring comes early there.

p.src: Silver blossoms and fiery trees make a city without night; on solid earth appears an isle of Penglai bright.

u.src: Silver blossoms and fiery trees make a city without night; on solid earth appears an isle of Penglai bright.

p.src: The Torch Dragon holds the light, and coldly gleams the night; the people sing and dance, rejoicing in peaceful times.

u.src: The Torch Dragon holds the light, and coldly gleams the night; the people sing and dance, rejoicing in peaceful times.

p.src: Five phoenix plumes uphold the paired shell gates; six giant turtles bear the three divine peaks.

u.src: Five phoenix plumes uphold the paired shell gates; six giant turtles bear the three divine peaks.

p.src: Rouged beauties stand beneath vermilion blinds; fair-faced youths ride purple steeds.

u.src: Rouged beauties stand beneath vermilion blinds; fair-faced youths ride purple steeds.

p.src: Shrill pipes and flutes resound into the azure clouds; clear moonbeams shine upon mandarin-duck tiles.

u.src: Shrill pipes and flutes resound into the azure clouds; clear moonbeams shine upon mandarin-duck tiles.

p.src: Green Cloud Tower rises high into the blue heavens; among the passing revelers are beauties beyond count.

u.src: Green Cloud Tower rises high into the blue heavens; among the passing revelers are beauties beyond count.

p.src: Lantern globes blaze brilliantly like embroidered brocade; princes and noble youths seem immortals indeed.

u.src: Lantern globes blaze brilliantly like embroidered brocade; princes and noble youths seem immortals indeed.

p.src: The tangled stream of revelers has not yet ceased, when suddenly clouds of smoke rise from the lofty tower.

p.src: That night, prison warden Cai Fu instructed his brother Cai Qing to watch the jail. “I shall go home for a look and return shortly.” He had only just entered his gate when two men slipped in after him: the first dressed as a military officer, the second like a servant. Looking at them by the lamplight, Cai Fu recognized the first as Chai Jin, the Little Whirlwind, and the man behind him was none other than Yue He, the Iron-Throated Songster. Warden Cai knew only Chai Jin. He invited them into the inner room and at once entertained them with food and wine already at hand. Chai Jin said, “There is no need to offer us wine. I have come with an urgent favor to ask. Councilor Lu and Shi Xiu have both received such care from you that our gratitude is beyond words. Tonight I wish to take advantage of the Lantern Festival bustle to pay them a visit in the prison. I beg you to trouble yourself to lead me inside, and not refuse me.” Cai Fu was an experienced officer and had already guessed most of their purpose. He was minded to refuse, yet truly feared that if the city were stormed, no good would come of it and the lives of his entire household, old and young, would be imperiled. He had no choice but to shoulder the blood-deep risk. Taking out some old clothes, he had the two men change into them, dressed them as officers with different headcloths, and led Chai Jin and Yue He straight to the prison.

p.src: Around the first watch, the three country couples—Wang the Short Tiger and One-Bolt Green, Sun Xin and Mistress Gu, Zhang Qing and Sun Erniang—disguised themselves thoroughly as village folk, mingled with the crowd, and entered by the eastern gate. Gongsun Sheng took Ling Zhen with him, carrying wicker baskets on a shoulder pole, and sat beneath the gallery of the City God Temple. (The City God Temple stood right beside the prefectural offices.) Zou Yuan and Zou Run carried lanterns and strolled idly about the city. Du Qian and Song Wan each pushed a cart straight to the front of Grand Secretary Liang's residence and slipped into the bustling crowd. (Grand Secretary Liang's residence was on the main avenue just inside the eastern gate.) Liu Tang and Yang Xiong each carried a constable's staff and concealed hidden weapons on their persons; they took seats on opposite sides of the prefectural bridge. Yan Qing led Zhang Shun into the city through the water gate and lay in ambush in a secluded place. Of these arrangements, no more need be said.

p.src: Before long, the drum atop the tower sounded the second watch. Now Shi Qian tucked a basket under his arm, filled with sulfur, saltpeter, and other incendiary materials, with several festive goose ornaments stuck atop it, and slipped behind Green Cloud Tower. He went upstairs and saw pipes and flutes playing in the private rooms, with drums and clappers sounding. The festivities were in full tumult, and young revelers thronged the upper floor, romping and admiring the lanterns. Once upstairs, Shi Qian pretended to be selling the goose ornaments and went around peering into every private room. He encountered Xie Zhen and Xie Bao wandering before the rooms with steel forks over their shoulders, rabbits hanging from the prongs. Shi Qian said, “The appointed hour has come. Why is there still no movement outside?” Xie Zhen replied, “We were just in front of the tower and saw a scout ride past. The troops have most likely arrived. Go ahead and do your part.” Before he had finished speaking, shouts erupted before the tower: “The Liangshan Marsh army has reached the western gate!” Xie Zhen told Shi Qian, “Hurry and go. I shall head to the Pacification Commissioner's office to support the others.” When he reached the Pacification Commissioner's office, he saw defeated and battered troops streaming into the city together, crying, “Wen the Great Broadsword's camp has been raided! The Liangshan Marsh outlaws have led their whole army to the city walls!” Li Cheng was patrolling atop the walls. When he heard the report, he galloped to the Pacification Commissioner's office, ordered the troops mustered, and commanded that the city gates be shut and the prefecture defended.

p.src: Meanwhile, Governor Wang personally led more than a hundred attendants, armed with long cangues and iron chains, to keep order in the streets. On hearing this report, he hurried in alarm to the Pacification Commissioner's office.

p.src: Grand Secretary Liang, meanwhile, was sitting idly and drunkenly before his residence. When the first report came, he was not yet greatly alarmed. But in less than half a watch, urgent mounted scouts came one after another with reports. Terrified out of his wits, he hastily ordered his horse made ready.

p.src: Before the words were out, fierce flames shot skyward from Green Cloud Tower, their glare outshining the moon in a tremendous blaze. At the sight, Grand Secretary Liang hurriedly mounted his horse. Just as he was about to go and investigate, he saw two great fellows push two carts into the middle of the road. They took down the bowl-hung lanterns, set the carts alight with them, and flames immediately sprang up. As Grand Secretary Liang tried to leave by the eastern gate, the two great fellows shouted, “Li Ying and Shi Jin are here!” Gripping their broad-bladed swords, they came striding forward to kill. The government troops guarding the gate fled in terror, while more than a dozen within reach were wounded. At that very moment Du Qian and Song Wan came out to meet them. The four joined forces and seized control of the eastern gate. Seeing that matters had gone awry, Grand Secretary Liang led his attendants in a headlong dash toward the southern gate. From the southern gate came the report: “A huge fat monk is whirling an iron Chan staff; and a tiger-faced pilgrim, wielding a pair of戒 swords, has charged into the city with a battle cry.” Grand Secretary Liang wheeled his horse and returned to the Pacification Commissioner's office, only to see Xie Zhen and Xie Bao there with steel forks in hand, charging this way and that; he urgently wished to return to the prefectural offices, but dared not go near them. Just then Governor Wang came past. Liu Tang and Yang Xiong brought down their two constables' staffs together, smashing out his brains and making his eyeballs bulge; he died there in the street. The aides and warders all fled to save what remained of their lives. Grand Secretary Liang hastily turned his horse and raced toward the western gate. Suddenly, cannon blasts erupted together from the City God Temple, roaring to heaven and shaking the earth. Zou Yuan and Zou Run held bamboo poles and went from eave to eave setting the houses ablaze. Before the southern entertainment quarter, Wang the Short Tiger and One-Bolt Green came charging and killing. Sun Xin and Mistress Gu drew the concealed weapons from their persons and joined in to assist them. Before the Bronze Buddha Temple, Zhang Qing and Sun Erniang went inside, climbed the lantern mountain, and set it on fire. By then, the common people within Beijing were scurrying like rats and fleeing like wolves; from every household rose wails fit to move gods and ghosts. Flames towered into the sky at more than a dozen places on every side, until no one could tell one direction from another.

p.src: Meanwhile, Grand Secretary Liang fled to the western gate, where he met Li Cheng's troops, then hurried to the southern gate. Reining in his horse, he looked out from the drum tower and saw the ground below packed with soldiers and cavalry. Their banners read: “The great general Huyan Zhuo.” Amid the blaze, he summoned his spirit and displayed his formidable valor. Han Tao was on his left, Peng Qi on his right, and Huang Xin behind; driving their forces onward, they swept across like outspread wild-goose wings and soon reached the gate. Unable to leave the city, Grand Secretary Liang hid with Li Cheng beneath the northern gate. There they saw flames blazing brightly and troops beyond counting: it was “Panther Head” Lin Chong, galloping forward with his spear leveled, Ma Lin on his left, Deng Fei on his right, and Hua Rong behind, urging the forces into a headlong charge. Turning again toward the eastern gate, amid an unbroken mass of torches they saw “Unrestrained” Mu Hong, with Du Xing on his left and Zheng Tianshou on his right. The three infantry heroes led the way, gripping their broad-bladed swords, and brought more than a thousand men charging into the city. Grand Secretary Liang made straight for the southern gate, risking his life to force a path of escape. Beside the drawbridge, torches flared all at once, revealing “Black Whirlwind” Li Kui, with Li Li on his left and Cao Zheng on his right. Li Kui had stripped to the skin. Clenching his teeth and wielding an axe in each hand, he came charging through the city moat; Li Li and Cao Zheng arrived at the same moment. Li Cheng took the lead, hacked open a blood-soaked path, broke out of the city, and fled while guarding Grand Secretary Liang. Suddenly battle cries thundered on their left. Amid countless troops and a forest of torches came Guan Sheng of the Great Sword, spurring his Red Hare and brandishing his Green Dragon blade as he charged straight at Grand Secretary Liang. Li Cheng raised his twin swords and advanced to meet him. But Li Cheng had no heart to prolong the fight; he wheeled his horse and fled. Xuan Zan charged in from the left and Hao Siwen from the right, striking at both flanks. Sun Li followed behind, driving his troops forward to join the assault. While the fighting raged, “Little Li Guang” Hua Rong overtook them from behind, drew his bow, set an arrow, and shot Li Cheng's deputy, who toppled from his horse. At the sight, Li Cheng galloped away. Before they had gone half an arrow's flight, gongs and drums erupted on their right and firelight dazzled their eyes. It was “Thunderbolt” Qin Ming, leaping forward on horseback and brandishing his mace, with Yan Shun and Ou Peng in his train; and from behind, Yang Zhi also came charging upon them. Li Cheng fought as he retreated, losing more than half his men, but managed to guard Grand Secretary Liang, break through the lines, and escape.

p.src: The tale now divides; let us speak of events within the city. Du Qian and Song Wan went to kill every member of Grand Secretary Liang's household, high and low alike. Liu Tang and Yang Xiong went to kill Governor Wang's entire family. Kong Ming and Kong Liang had already scaled the rear wall of the prison office and entered. Zou Yuan and Zou Run stood before the prison office, intercepting anyone who came or went. In the main prison, Chai Jin and Yue He saw the signal fire rise. Chai Jin said to Cai Fu and Cai Qing, “You two brothers see it, do you not? What are you waiting for?” When Cai Qing looked from the doorway, Zou Yuan and Zou Run had already smashed open the prison gate and were shouting, “All the heroes of Liangshan Marsh are here! Bring out our brothers, Squire Lu and Shi Xiu, peaceably!” As Cai Qing hurried to inform Cai Fu, Kong Ming and Kong Liang were already leaping down from the prison roof. Without regard for whether the two brothers consented, Chai Jin produced weapons concealed on his person, removed the cangues, and freed Lu Junyi and Shi Xiu. Chai Jin told Cai Fu, “Come quickly with me to my home and protect my family!” Together they all came out through the prison gate. Zou Yuan and Zou Run met them, and the parties joined forces. Cai Fu and Cai Qing followed Chai Jin to his home and kept his family safe.

p.src: Lu Junyi led Shi Xiu and the five brothers Kong Ming, Kong Liang, Zou Yuan, and Zou Run straight to his home to seize Li Gu and Lady Jia. Now Li Gu had heard that the heroes of Liangshan Marsh had led their forces into the city, and he saw fires rising on every side. Uneasy at home, his eyelid twitching ominously, he conferred with Lady Jia, gathered a bundle of gold, pearls, and valuables, slung it over his back, and fled through the door. They heard the row of street doors crash down, as an unknown multitude came surging inside. Li Gu and Lady Jia hurriedly turned back, opened the rear gate, slipped along the wall, and went straight down to the river in search of their private hiding place. Then Zhang Shun shouted from the bank, “Where do you think you're going, woman?” Li Gu panicked and jumped into a boat to hide. Just as he tried to squeeze into the cabin, a hand reached out, seized him by the beard, and a voice demanded, “Li Gu, do you recognize me?” Recognizing Yan Qing's voice, Li Gu cried in alarm, “Brother Xiao Yi, there has never been any grudge between us! Do not drag me ashore!” On the bank, Zhang Shun had already tucked the woman beneath his arm and dragged her to the boat. Yan Qing seized Li Gu, and they all headed toward the eastern gate.

For the moment, he ordered his men to load all the household property, gold, silver, and treasures onto carts, to be taken to Liangshan Marsh and distributed. Chai Jin and Cai Fu, meanwhile, went to the house, gathered up the family and property, and prepared to take them all to the mountain stronghold. p.src: Smoke shrouded the city; flames consumed its towers. In the crimson glow, glazed tiles shattered; amid black flames, kingfisher-green ornaments burned. The puppets made for amusement could no longer tell front from back; as for the festival scaffolds that lit the night, who cared which side was bright and which was dark? White-whiskered elders with mottled hair ran madly about until beard and mustache were singed away; young men with glossy black hair fled, abandoning even their splendid parasols. Those who rode hobbyhorses met blades and spears in the darkness; those who danced the Baolao could not escape sword and lance. Flower-fair ladies saw gold fall and jade shatter amid the crowd; beauties who had come to admire the sights scattered in moments like stars and clouds. Alas, a place of song and dance for a thousand years had become one vast battlefield.

p.src: By then broad daylight had come, and within the city Wu Yong and Chai Jin sounded the gong to recall the troops. The chieftains welcomed Squire Lu and Shi Xiu, and all met at the military governor's office. The two men related in detail how they owed their surviving lives to the care of the brothers Cai Fu and Cai Qing in prison. Yan Qing and Zhang Shun had already brought Li Gu and Lady Jia under guard. When Lu Junyi saw them, he ordered Yan Qing to confine and personally guard them pending judgment. Of this, no more need be said.

p.src: Meanwhile, Li Cheng was escorting Grand Secretary Liang from the city to escape the disaster when they encountered Wen Da returning with the remnants of his defeated forces. Joining their troops, they fled southward. As they went, a battle cry rose from their vanguard. It was “Demon King Who Roils the World” Fan Rui, with Xiang Chong on his left and Li Gun on his right.
